fields.narrative_intro: *A seething person and a preening person discuss OpenCode's leaked user credentials inside a broken time machine stuck between two eras.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
SEETHING PERSON: "OpenCode was hacked; user credentials leaked."
PREENING PERSON: "Change the password."
fields.panel2:
[build]
SEETHING PERSON: "I did. The machine asks which era."
PREENING PERSON: "Choose the future."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SEETHING PERSON: "It says the leak already arrived yesterday."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The time machine flashes CREDENTIALS LEAKED across its PAST and FUTURE displays.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
PREENING PERSON: "Reset them!"
SEETHING PERSON: "Already did. The reset takes effect yesterday."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The machine ejects a receipt: PASSWORD RESET — SUCCESSFUL — ACCOUNT STILL LOGGED IN.]

narrative_summary: A broken time machine turns OpenCode's credential leak into a password reset that takes effect yesterday.
rationale: Candidate 3 has the cleanest escalation and strongest closing reversal: a password reset that takes effect yesterday, followed by the visual confirmation that the account remains logged in. It uses the time-machine premise without leaning on the more familiar leak-across-two-eras framing.
place: inside a broken time machine stuck between two eras
hat_pair: foam cardboard box worn as a cube helmet with FRAGILE stamped on every face
foam bowling pin hat with three red stripes
